sketch_steps: Fix f and the given derivative u at a.
Evaluate the outer function at the correct base point f(a).
The outer derivative is defined at every real input.
Apply the arctan chain rule and retain the inner derivative factor u.

typed-calculus-v3.proof_strategy: Expand the degree-n Taylor polynomial as the sum of coefficients of orders k≤n.
sketch_steps: Expand the degree-n Taylor polynomial as the sum of coefficients of orders k≤n.
The k-th within derivative of x^(n+1) is a falling-factorial coefficient times x^(n+1-k).
Every exponent n+1-k is positive, so each coefficient at zero vanishes.
The Taylor value is zero while positivity of b gives a strictly positive actual function value, for every n including zero.

Multiply by the positive secant denominator to obtain f(a)≤f(x).
For x<a bound the reversed secant slope from above by zero and obtain the same conclusion.
At x=a equality completes the global comparison.

Its evaluation at f equals the evaluation of the lower-degree remainder.
Minimality forces an annihilating remainder to vanish.
Conversely any multiple annihilates f by the evaluation homomorphism.

typed-linear-algebra-v6.proof_strategy: A basis provides both independent vectors and a spanning family.
sketch_steps: A basis provides both independent vectors and a spanning family.
Conversely spanning gives a representation of each vector.
Independence makes that representation unique.
The representation equivalence constructs a basis with exactly the supplied vectors.

sketch_steps: Set f(x,y)=c when x=0 and zero otherwise.
The exceptional hyperplane has product measure zero, so f is almost everywhere zero and integrable.
Its section at x=0 is the nonzero constant c.
Lebesgue measure of positive-dimensional ℝⁿ is infinite, hence that constant section is not integrable.

For ordered endpoints it is the outward flux through the rectangle; the algebraic identity also holds for reversed or degenerate endpoint choices.

sketch_steps: Pair the top and bottom integrals, whose x-dependent and constant terms cancel.
Their difference is δ times the height times the width.
Pair the right and left integrals; their difference is α times the width times the height.
Add the two contributions to obtain the trace coefficient α+δ times signed area.
